description: Given an n x n grid of 0s and 1s, construct a Quad-Tree representation. If all values in a region are the same, it is a leaf. Otherwise, divide into four quadrants and recurse.
examples:
Input: grid = [[0,1],[1,0]]
Output: a Quad-Tree with four leaf children
intuition: A Quad-Tree recursively divides a grid into four quadrants. If all values in a region are the same, collapse it into a single leaf. Otherwise, recurse on each quadrant. It is like a compression scheme - uniform regions get simplified.
approach: Recursively build the four quadrants down to individual cells. If all four child nodes are leaves with the same value, collapse them into one leaf. Otherwise, return an internal node with those children. Each merge checks only the four child results.
jsWalkthrough:
Example: grid = [[0,1],[1,0]]

build(0,0,2):
  halfSize=1
  topLeft  = build(0,0,1): grid[0][0]=0 → Node(false, leaf)
  topRight = build(0,1,1): grid[0][1]=1 → Node(true,  leaf)
  botLeft  = build(1,0,1): grid[1][0]=1 → Node(true,  leaf)
  botRight = build(1,1,1): grid[1][1]=0 → Node(false, leaf)

  allLeaves=true, but 0≠1 → not allSameValue
  → return internal Node with 4 leaf children
explanation:
1. Base case: size 1, create a leaf with the cell value.
2. Recursively build four quadrant nodes.
3. If all four are leaves with the same value, merge into a single leaf.
4. Otherwise, create an internal node with four children.
hints: Divide the grid into four equal quadrants recursively.
If all cells in a quadrant have the same value, it is a leaf.
Merge four identical leaves into one.

timeComplexityBreakdown.variables: n = grid side length; there are n² cells.

phases.label: Create leaves for the individual cells
Combine groups of four on all higher levels

timeComplexityBreakdown.note: This code builds children first and compares four child results. It does not rescan each square at every level. The higher-level work is a geometric series, not n² work on every level.
